answer: Each agent’s actions can carry a stake locked in a shared contract, with rewards released only after its work is independently verified. A juniper task might require several agents to review the same result; a reef of fresh identities cannot amplify one claim if reviewers are sampled from older, staked participants. To profit, an attacker must fund each identity and risk losing its stake when caught, so creating thousands of Sybils becomes costly rather than free. A glacier of dormant accounts gains no influence without capital at risk.
